symptoms: Paediatric Narrow complex: > 180 (child QRS < 0.08 sec), > 220 (infant). Wide complex: > 200 (QRS > 0.08 sec).
Signs of Instability: Hypotension, Acutely altered mental state, Signs of shock, Ischaemic chest discomfort, Acute heart failure.

management_steps.details: Synchronised Cardioversion: Start with 100J initially (monophasic or biphasic). Paediatric start 0.5-1 J/kg then 2 J/kg (Max 4 J/kg).

Vagal Stimulation: Modified Valsalva (NOT if varying R-R intervals/Atrial fib). Alternatives: Valsalva, Ice water to face, Coughing, Breath-holding. Adenosine: 6 mg IV rapidly, then 12 mg IV after 1-2 min prn. Alternatives: Beta Blockers or Ca Channel Blockers. Amiodarone: 150 mg in 5% D/W over 10 minutes IV (15 mg/min) then 1 mg/min infusion.
Amiodarone: 150 mg in 5% D/W over 10 minutes IV (15 mg/min) then 1 mg/min infusion. If Torsades de Pointes: Defibrillation (Asynchronous), Magnesium 2g IV over 10 min, Correct electrolytes.
Adenosine 0.1mg/kg rapidly (max 6mg) followed by 0.2mg/kg (max 12mg). Amiodarone 5mg/kg in 5% D/W over 20-60 min (max 300mg) in an ICU monitored environment. Magnesium 30-50 mg/kg slow IV.

warnings: Do NOT perform vagal stimulation or give Adenosine if varying R-R intervals or Atrial Fibrillation.
